p-value for Age = 0.0025 (Wald test; exact value 0.0024995441).

In the combined logistic regression of treatment response on BMI, Age, and Gender (PR = 1 for partial response vs PD/SD = 0; N = 80), the age coefficient is negative and statistically significant: age coefficient = -0.0795 log-odds per year, SE = 0.0263, z = -3.023, p = 0.0025, 95% CI [-0.131, -0.028]. This means older age is associated with lower odds of PR, adjusting for BMI and gender.
